sha.description:
SHA is the commit to report on. Empty reads HEAD from the checkout,
which is the commit git-commit made and git-push published.

path.description:
Path is the checkout to read the repository and HEAD from, relative to
the Passage work dir.

repo.description:
Repo overrides the repository URL. Empty reads it from the checkout's
origin remote.

provider.description: Provider is `github` or `gitlab`. Empty is inferred from the host.

baseURL.description:
BaseURL is the API root, for GitHub Enterprise Server and self-managed
GitLab.

context.description:
Context names the check. Empty is `hecate/<gate>`, so two Gates reporting
on the same commit do not overwrite each other.

state.description:
State overrides the outcome. Empty reports what actually happened, which
is almost always what you want; set `Pending` on a step at the top of a
Passage to show the crossing has started.

targetURL.description: TargetURL is where a human goes for detail.

credentialsRef.description:
CredentialsRef names a Secret holding an API token, or a GitHub App's
keys. Required: reporting a status needs API access, which is not the
same thing as push access.

commit-status.description: CommitStatusConfig is the `with:` block of a commit-status step.

path.description:
Path is the file to edit, relative to the Passage work dir — so a file in
the default checkout is `repo/apps/prod/values.yaml`.

value.description: Value is a string, number or boolean.

items.description: FieldEdit sets one field to one value.

edits.description: Edits are applied in order, all or nothing.

edit-yaml.description: EditYAMLConfig is the `with:` block of an edit-yaml step.

gates.description:
Gates selects which checks apply. Empty runs none, which is a mistake
worth reporting rather than a quiet pass.

A dev Gate can run none of them and production all four.

policy.description:
Policy is the Fides policy name for the `assert` gate. Empty asks Fides
for every policy that applies to the artifact.

maxRisk.description:
MaxRisk fails the crossing when the change gate's risk score exceeds it,
letting a team be stricter than Fides' own verdict. 0-100.

reportArtifacts.description:
ReportArtifacts records every image digest in the Bundle against the
trail, so a change gate sees the whole release rather than the one
artifact whose trail was looked up.

Off by default, and deliberately: Fides upserts on the digest and
overwrites the trail link, so this claims the other images belong to
*this* trail. That is true when one CI run built them all and wrong when
they came from different builds — which only the operator knows.

holdTimeout.description:
HoldTimeout bounds how long a held change may wait before the crossing
fails. Default 24h.

pollInterval.description: PollInterval is how often a held change is re-read. Default 1m.

evidence-gate.description: EvidenceGateConfig is the `with:` block of an evidence-gate step.

apiVersion.description: APIVersion overrides the default for Kind.

namespace.description: Namespace defaults to the Gate's namespace.

resources.description:
Resources are the Flux objects to nudge — usually the GitRepository the
commit went to, and sometimes the Kustomization that consumes it.

clusterRef.description:
ClusterRef names a Secret holding a kubeconfig for the cluster these
resources live in. Empty is the cluster Hecate runs in.

The same field flux-wait and the Flux health check take, and it is here
so a Gate can nudge the cluster it then waits on. Without it a remote
promotion could be waited for but not prompted, so it moved at the remote
Flux's own interval while the local one was nudged — the asymmetry showed
up as remote environments simply being slower, for no reason anyone could
see in the Gate.

The namespace rule is not relaxed by crossing a cluster boundary: a step
that can annotate any namespace's Kustomization can trigger any tenant's
deployment, and that is as true remotely as locally.

flux-reconcile.description: FluxReconcileConfig is the `with:` block of a flux-reconcile step.

apiVersion.description: APIVersion overrides the default for Kind.

namespace.description: Namespace defaults to the Gate's namespace.

resources.description: Resources are the Flux objects to assess.

expectedRevision.description:
ExpectedRevision, when set, requires Flux to have applied this revision.
Usually wired from an earlier step: ${{ steps.commit.sha }}.

failAfter.description:
FailAfter is a Go duration bounding how long a resource may be un-Ready
before it is reported Degraded rather than Progressing. Default 10m.

clusterRef.description:
ClusterRef names a Secret holding a kubeconfig for the cluster these
resources live in. Empty is the cluster Hecate runs in.

The namespace rule is unchanged by this: a Gate in `team-a` watching a
remote cluster is still restricted to `team-a` there. Otherwise a
cluster reference becomes the way around the tenant boundary (#85, D11)
— add a kubeconfig, watch everything everywhere.

+optional

flux-wait.description: FluxConfig is the `with:` block of a Flux health check.

repo.description: Repo is the repository to clone, as an HTTPS URL.

branch.description:
Branch is what to check out. Empty clones the repository's default
branch; naming one also limits the clone to that branch alone.

path.description: Path is where the working tree goes, relative to the Passage work dir.

depth.description:
Depth limits history. Zero clones everything; 1 is enough to commit on
top of the tip and is much faster on a large repository.

credentialsRef.description:
CredentialsRef names a Secret holding the credential to clone with. A
public repository needs none.

git-clone.description: GitCloneConfig is the `with:` block of a git-clone step.

path.description: Path is the checkout to commit in, relative to the Passage work dir.

paths.description: Paths limits what is staged. Empty stages every change.

allowEmpty.description:
AllowEmpty commits even with no changes. Off by default: an empty commit
usually means an earlier edit step did nothing, which is worth noticing
rather than burying under a commit that changes no files.

git-commit.description: GitCommitConfig is the `with:` block of a git-commit step.

path.description:
Path is the checkout to read the repository and base branch from,
relative to the Passage work dir.

repo.description:
Repo overrides the repository URL. Empty reads it from the checkout's
origin remote, which is where git-clone put it.

provider.description:
Provider is `github` or `gitlab`. Empty is inferred from the host, which
only works for the public hosts — an appliance must say which it is.

baseURL.description:
BaseURL is the API root, for GitHub Enterprise Server and self-managed
GitLab.

head.description:
Head is the branch to merge. Empty uses the branch git-push creates with
`toNewBranch`, so the common flow needs no wiring.

base.description:
Base is the branch to merge into. Empty uses the checked-out branch,
which is the one git-clone was pointed at.

title.description: Title is the pull request's title. Empty is generated from the Passage.

body.description: Body is the description. Empty is generated from what is being promoted.

labels.description: Labels are applied on creation. A label added later is not removed.

waitForMerge.description:
WaitForMerge holds the Passage open until the pull request merges.

A pointer so that not saying anything means true. A crossing that
succeeds the moment a pull request opens would mark the Bundle as having
cleared the environment before any human looked at it, which is the
opposite of what asking for review means.

pollInterval.description: PollInterval overrides how often an open pull request is re-read.

credentialsRef.description:
CredentialsRef names a Secret holding an API token, or a GitHub App's
keys. Opening a pull request needs API access, which push access alone
does not give.

git-pull-request.description: GitPullRequestConfig is the `with:` block of a git-pull-request step.

path.description: Path is the checkout to push from, relative to the Passage work dir.

branch.description: Branch overrides the target branch. Empty pushes the checked-out branch.

toNewBranch.description:
ToNewBranch pushes to a fresh branch named after the Passage, for flows
that open a pull request rather than committing to the trunk.

force.description:
Force pushes even when the remote branch has moved on, discarding what is
there. Off by default, because on a shared branch that is someone else's
work.

credentialsRef.description:
CredentialsRef names a Secret holding the credential to push with. Push
access, which is not the same thing as the API token a status or pull
request needs.

git-push.description: GitPushConfig is the `with:` block of a git-push step.

method.description: Method defaults to GET, or POST when a body is given.

headers.description:
Headers are sent as written. Put nothing secret here: a Gate is a normal
object that anyone with read access can see.

prefix.description: Prefix goes in front of the secret value, for schemes like "Bearer ".

key.description: Key in the Secret. Defaults to "token".

items.description: SecretHeader is one header whose value comes from a Secret.

secretHeaders.description:
SecretHeaders are read from Secrets at call time, which is where a token
belongs.

expectStatus.description: ExpectStatus lists acceptable status codes. Empty accepts any 2xx.

successIf.description:
SuccessIf is a condition over `status`, `body` and `json`, evaluated
after the response arrives.

Written without `${{ }}`, because those are substituted before the step
runs and there is no response yet at that point.

timeout.description:
Timeout bounds the call. Empty is 30 seconds, so a hung endpoint does not
hold a worker.

http.description: HTTPConfig is the `with:` block of an http step.

tag.description: Tag or Digest identifies what to pull. A digest is exact; a tag can move.

digest.description: Digest pins exactly. Set this or Tag, not both.

out.description: Out is where to unpack it, relative to the Passage work dir.

insecure.description:
Insecure allows a plain-HTTP registry. Always opt-in: falling back
silently would send registry credentials in clear.

credentialsRef.description:
CredentialsRef names a Secret holding registry credentials. Empty uses the
ambient keychain, which is what a workload identity provides.

oci-pull.description: OCIPullConfig is the `with:` block of an oci-pull step.

path.description: Path is the directory to package, relative to the Passage work dir.

repo.description: Repo is the target repository, e.g. ghcr.io/acme/manifests.

tag.description: Tag is what to publish it as.

source.description:
Source and Revision are recorded as annotations, and are what an
OCIRepository reports as the revision it applied — so this is what makes
a deployment traceable back to what produced it.

revision.description: Revision is what an OCIRepository reports as the revision it applied.

insecure.description:
Insecure allows a plain-HTTP registry. Always opt-in: falling back
silently would send registry credentials in clear.

credentialsRef.description:
CredentialsRef names a Secret holding registry credentials. Empty uses the
ambient keychain, which is what a workload identity provides.

oci-push.description: OCIPushConfig is the `with:` block of an oci-push step.

chart.description:
Chart is the chart directory, relative to the Passage work dir.

A directory in the checkout, not a repository reference: what is rendered
has to be what was reviewed, and a chart pulled at render time could
differ between the pull request and the crossing.

out.description: Out is where to write the rendered YAML, relative to the work dir.

valuesFiles.description: ValuesFiles are values files to apply in order, relative to the work dir.

values.description: Values are inline values, applied last so a step can override a file.

releaseName.description: ReleaseName is the release the templates see as .Release.Name.

namespace.description:
Namespace is what the templates see as .Release.Namespace. Empty uses the
Gate's own namespace, which is the usual intent.

includeCRDs.description:
IncludeCRDs renders the chart's crds/ directory too. Off by default,
matching `helm template`.

kubeVersion.description:
KubeVersion is what .Capabilities.KubeVersion reports. Empty uses Helm's
default rather than the cluster's: rendering must not depend on which
cluster the controller happens to be running in, or the same commit would
render differently in two places.

apiVersions.description:
APIVersions is what .Capabilities.APIVersions reports, for charts that
branch on whether an API is available.

render-helm.description: RenderHelmConfig is the `with:` block of a render-helm step.

path.description: Path is the kustomization directory, relative to the Passage work dir.

out.description:
Out is where to write the rendered YAML, relative to the work dir. It is
a file, not a directory: the whole build is one document stream, and
splitting it per resource would make the git diff a rename storm the
first time anything is reordered.

loadRestrictionsNone.description:
LoadRestrictionsNone allows the kustomization to reference files outside
its own directory.

Off by default, matching kustomize's own default and Flux's: a build that
can read anywhere in the checkout can read a file the author did not mean
to publish.

render-kustomize.description: RenderKustomizeConfig is the `with:` block of a render-kustomize step.

path.description: Path is the kustomization to edit, relative to the Passage work dir.

image.description:
Image is the repository to repin, matched against the `name:` of an entry
in the file's `images:` list.

tag.description:
Tag and Digest are what to pin it to. Leave both empty to take them from
the Bundle being promoted, which is the usual case.

digest.description: Digest pins exactly, where a tag can be moved under you.

set-image.description: SetImageConfig is the `with:` block of a set-image step.
